Máté Marjai

Engineering leader with 18+ years in payments and fintech. At Primer I lead two teams in the Orchestration org, one through an Engineering Manager who reports to me, across iOS, Android, Web and backend. I grew a Senior Engineer into the company's only home-grown EM in over two years, and built engineering-wide mechanisms that other teams adopted: a testing standard, incident fire drills, AI-assisted engineering tooling and hiring practices. I tie engineering work to business outcomes such as checkout conversion, load time and cost. Earlier: two seed-stage CTO roles, founder of a payments engineering consultancy, and founding engineer of SumUp's Dublin team (0 to 15 engineers).

Engineering Manager, Orchestration (Conversion & Payment Operations) at Primer

Feb 2024 - Present

Key Achievements

Series C payments platform. I lead two teams. Conversion owns the merchant checkout SDKs on iOS, Android and Web, and I run it through an Engineering Manager who reports to me. Payment Operations owns payment state, timeline and search services, and I lead it directly. Before the split I grew and led the 12-engineer Experience team.

  • Org design: designed the split of Experience into Conversion and a net-new Payment Operations team, held the design through exec review, then hired the Conversion EM and handed the team over to him within four weeks. Introduced a delegated Tech Lead model that other teams adopted.
  • Growing leaders: grew a Senior Engineer into an EM over 18 months, wrote the ramp-up and Associate EM path the org now uses, grew another engineer to Staff, turned an underperformer into the Android lead, and took two engineers through promotion.
  • Business impact: led the Checkout SDK rearchitecture, cutting merchant integration time from weeks to hours. Found that a top merchant's 9-second checkout load time was an outlier and drove the fix (median 2.2s to 0.3s, P95 3.9s to 1.8s; platform median now under 400ms). Their move to the new checkout delivered a 1.17% conversion uplift.
  • Engineering-wide mechanisms: authored the company's engineering testing standard; created incident fire drills, which other EMs now run from my framework; built an AI on-call assistant adopted by two other teams; and rolled out AI-assisted code review across SDK and backend repos.
  • Hiring system: rewrote the EM job spec, redesigned the frontend hiring challenge, and shipped an AI interview-evaluation tool, calibrated to the competency matrix, to every EM.
  • Exec and merchant escalations: represented engineering in high-stakes merchant escalations alongside the exec team. I reframed headline claims with data, established the real root cause so commercial decisions rested on facts, and kept urgent demands inside the normal escalation process so no single merchant could set the priorities for everyone else.
  • Reliability and cost: wrote the backend on-call guidance and split the on-call rota across teams; cut the escalation backlog from 100+ tickets to a 1–2 week steady state. On cost: localisation into 22 languages with AI tooling for about $3.6k less than the alternative, and an infrastructure tier decision worth about $24k a year.
  • Culture: no regretted attrition over 16 months, 9+/10 on manager impact in the culture survey, and the team at industry P90 on developer experience scores. Rebooted the engineering blog and wrote its first article.
